latin: Quiditates habent ab aeterno suum esse formale a se, non ab extrinseco.
translation: Quiddities have their formal being from eternity of themselves, not from something extrinsic.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch5, from Latin at farmer1998:11987
attribution: Reports Francis of Meyronnes, on quiddities as ideas in the divine mind (farmer1998:11969, 12056).

sources.text: Francis of Meyronnes, Scriptum super Primum Sententiarum, pp. x9v-y1r, on Sentences 1, distinction 42, question 2 ('whether quiddities ... have existence from eternity of themselves and not from an external cause')
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit cites this passage, already indicated by Farmer, as the source of the thesis.

doctrine: The thesis holds that 'quiddities' -- for Francis, the ideas in the mind of God -- 'formally hold their existence by themselves and from eternity, not by anything external' (edelheit2022:13351), and so do not 'require an external cause' (edelheit2022:13379). Farmer glosses 'quiddities' here as referring to the divine ideas, distinct from the material-essence sense of the term used elsewhere in the 900 (e.g. 2.42) and from the sense used of ideas reflected in the separate intelligences (e.g. 7.36), a distinction Farmer says Pico meant to rank hierarchically in his planned Roman debate (farmer1998:12056).
context: Farmer records that the thesis is 'opposed to' 4.2 from Scotus and 'strongly linked' to 5.9 from Henry of Ghent, and that 11>58 may bear further on Pico's own view of the same issue (farmer1998:12056).
historiography: Edelheit identifies the source discussion as Francis of Meyronnes's commentary on Sentences 1, distinction 42, question 2, citing Scriptum super Primum Sententiarum, pp. x9v-y1r, and notes that this identification 'was indicated by Farmer' (edelheit2022:13379).

quotations.text: In thesis 5 we learn that quiddities formally hold their existence by them- selves and from eternity, not by anything external.

not_established: not established by the sources consulted
